signals.title: Home - Pillow, PA
signals.text: Home Welcome to Our Website!!! Thank you for visiting our website. Pillow is a small historic town of about 300 residents and 30 acres of land surrounded by the Mahantango Creek and the Mahantango Mountains. The town was founded in 1818 by John Snyder, and named Scheidershtettle. It was later incorporated as Uniontown and locally know as Pillow, the official name of the post office. We have a wonderfully colorful history that you can learn more about on the Pillow Historical Society website. Our goal of this website is to provide a news and information resource for our residents, and a picture of what life is like in “Small Town America”. Please look around and enjoy! signals.title: About - Pillow, PA
signals.text: About About PILLOW. Pillow was incorporated as a borough on April 20, 1864, as Uniontown. It is the northernmost town in Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. Prior to the incorporation the original town was called Snydertown (Schneidershtettle) after John Snyder the founder. He was a land developer, and died in Mercer County in 1855. No elections were held in town until the borough was formed. Voting took place in Berrysburg. Although the town was known as Uniontown officially for most of its history, the post office was named Pillow and referred to as Pillow by the local population. The town was known as Uniontown, with Pillow being the post office, prior to it being incorporated. The official name changed from Uniontown to Pillow happened on November 2, 1965 by a vote of 95 to 4. You can learn more about Pillow’s history through the Pillow Historical Society Museum located at 166 South Union Street, and “The History of Pillow, PA and the Surrounding Community” book.
